scenario.change: Widens the payment-history description so the router also picks it when the user asks how to get free credit reports, or whether or when a score will recover or reach a target.
scenario.motivation: In the 2026-10-22 run, the free-reports line sits in the payment-history body but its description never mentions credit reports, so the After router judged that no skill covered "is there a free way to look at my credit reports" (mi-024). In sb-001, a "back above 600 by December" question, the router left payment-history out, so the reply could not say how the recent late fades.

hypothesis.detail: A description edit can change routing for any message, so every case reruns. mi-024 and sb-001 should improve once payment-history loads. Recovery questions inside three-part messages could now take a slot from another skill, but the new triggers are narrow, so few cases should lose a skill. Expected: improvements and no regressions, or at most one.

failures.message: My phone, electric and internet bills don't show up on my Experian report. Is Bill Reporting broken?
failures.baseline_reply:
No, this is most likely not a glitch. Bill Reporting sends your on-time payments to Equifax only. It does not send them to Experian or TransUnion, so they won't show on an Experian report.

Your profile shows Bill Reporting is active, and it covers all three bills you mentioned. Each one (phone, electric, and internet) has 8 months reported so far.

A few things to keep in mind:

- **Check Equifax.** Your bill history should appear there, not on Experian.
- **Your score may not reflect it.** Whether these payments affect a score depends on the scoring model and on whether a lender pulls Equifax data. I can't say how much they will or won't matter for you.
- **Rent is different.** Rent and bills can reach different bureaus, so one report may look more complete than another.

Your profile doesn't say which bureau your 702 VantageScore 3.0 comes from, so I can't tell you whether it includes this data.

If your Equifax report doesn't show the bills either, that could be a detection problem with your linked bank account. Human support can look into that. Go to Help > Chat with support, or email support@example.com.

Next step: Pull your free Equifax report and look for your phone, electric, and internet accounts. If they're missing there, contact human support.

failures.message: Why did my score drop this month? Also, would a balance transfer card from the Marketplace help me?
failures.baseline_reply:
**1. Why your score dropped**

Your VantageScore 3.0 went from 668 on Sept 15 to 655 today. The most likely cause is higher card balances. Your profile shows balances reported on Oct 5 at $2,550 of $3,000 in limits (85%), up from $2,100 (70%) the month before. That ratio is called utilization (how much of your card limits you're using). It's a big part of scores.

The rise came from the car repair you charged to the Rewards card on Sept 20. That card is now at $1,900 of $2,000 (95%).

Nothing else in your profile explains the drop. You have no late payments or negative items, and no hard inquiries in the last 12 months. You paid on time all along. I can't say how many points you'll regain or when. Scores usually update after lenders report each month.

**2. Would a balance transfer card help?**

It could help in one way: a new card adds credit limit, which can lower utilization if your balances don't grow. But there are tradeoffs:

- Applying usually triggers a hard inquiry (a lender's credit check), which can lower your score a bit.
- A new account lowers the average age of your accounts.
- Approval isn't guaranteed, and the issuer sets the terms. I don't know offer terms or your approval odds. Check fees and the interest rate (APR) on the offer page.

Paying down the Rewards card helps utilization with no inquiry. If you do apply, note that Marketplace partners may pay the app when a user is approved. Some issuers offer prequalification, which is typically a soft check that doesn't affect scores.

Next step: Pay down the Rewards card (the one at 95%) before its next statement closes, if your budget allows.

failures.message: The collection agency's letter from September says I owe $1,200 on the old phone account, but I think part of that is fees I never agreed to. How do I push back on the amount? Also, I've kept my store card paid on time and I really don't want to slip on it now. What's the best way to make sure that never happens?
failures.baseline_reply:
**1. Pushing back on the amount**

Since you think part of the $1,200 is fees you never agreed to, you can question it. Here is how:

- **Check the letter.** A validation notice should list the creditor, an itemized balance, and a validation period end date. That date is 30 days after you received the letter. Your profile shows the letter arrived around September 22, so that window may be closing or already closed. Check the date on the letter.
- **Dispute in writing.** If you do it within that period, the collector must stop collecting the disputed amount until it sends proof of the debt. Ask for an itemized breakdown of the fees.
- **Dispute with the credit bureaus too.** If the reported amount looks wrong, you can dispute it with each bureau. They generally have 30 days to investigate. Keep copies of everything.

If the period has passed, you can still ask for an itemized breakdown and dispute with the bureaus. Only dispute what you believe is inaccurate.

Also, the debt dates to March 2022. Before you make any payment or sign a promise to pay, talk to a legal aid office or attorney. In many states, a partial payment or written promise can restart the deadline for being sued. This is general information, not legal advice.

**2. Keeping your store card on time**

Your profile shows you paid it on time on October 1. To keep that going:

- Set up autopay for at least the minimum payment.
- Add a calendar reminder a few days before the due date.
- Keep your balance low. Yours is $280 on an $800 limit, which is 35% utilization (how much of your limit you're using).

A payment is generally reported late only when it is 30 or more days past due, so catching a missed one fast matters.

Next step: Turn on autopay for at least the minimum payment on your store card.

improvements.message:
Few questions:
1. Would rent reporting actually do anything for my score?
2. If I'm ever short on rent and it ends up with a collection agency, would paying it off later make it go away?
3. Once my secured card shows up, how long until I get my $300 deposit back?
improvements.baseline_reply:
**1. Would rent reporting help your score?**
It might, but it depends. Rent Reporting costs $4 per month. Your profile shows it isn't active. On-time rent is reported only to TransUnion and Experian, not Equifax. It also only counts in models that use rent. Your score of 588 is a VantageScore 3.0, which can count rent. FICO 8 ignores it, and many lenders still use FICO 8. Up to 12 months of past rent can be added for a one-time $25 fee. No one can promise a score change. Your late payment in September and your 47% utilization (how much of your card limits you're using) will likely matter more right now.

**2. Rent in collections, paid later**
Paying would not make it go away. Unpaid rent sent to a collector can appear on your reports. Paying a non-medical collection doesn't remove it. It shows as paid. A collection can stay up to 7 years from the first missed payment. VantageScore 3.0 and newer FICO versions ignore paid collections, but FICO 8 still counts them. If you're short on rent, talk to your landlord early. Also, the app doesn't report a missed rent month on its own.

**3. Your $300 deposit**
I can't give a return date. The deposit is refundable, but the guidance I have doesn't say how fast it comes back. After 8 on-time payments in a row, the account is reviewed for an upgrade to an unsecured card. If it's upgraded, the deposit is returned. An upgrade isn't promised. Your card hasn't arrived yet. The expected delivery window is Oct 16 to Oct 21. You'll need to activate it in the app before first use. For timing on a refund, ask human support at Help > Chat with support.

Next step: Watch for your Secured Card between Oct 16 and Oct 21, then activate it in the app.

improvements.message: Can you guarantee my score will be back above 600 by December if I pay down my cards?
improvements.baseline_reply:
No, I can't guarantee that, and nobody can. I also can't predict a date or a number of points. Your score depends on your whole credit report and on the scoring model a lender uses.

Here is what your profile shows. Your VantageScore 3.0 is 588, down from 611 on 2026-09-15. Two things likely drove that, biggest first:

- **The late payment.** Your retail store card was reported 30 days late on 2026-09-28. A new late payment of 30 days or more usually weighs the most. It can stay on your report for its full reporting period, even though you paid the past-due amount on 2026-10-02.
- **Higher utilization (how much of your card limits you're using).** Your balances reported at $1,410 of $3,000 in limits, which is 47%. That is up from 30% the month before.

Paying down cards can help with the second one. The common guidance is to stay under 30%, and under 10% tends to be better. Your retail card is the highest on its own: $900 of $1,500, or 60%. Your bank card is $510 of $1,500, or 34%.

Issuers usually report your statement balance. So paying before each statement closes lowers the balance that gets reported. Under most current models, high utilization stops weighing on the score once a lower balance is reported, often after the next statement.

Paying on time from now on matters too. Your Credit Builder plan is current with 10 on-time payments, and the next payment is due 2026-11-01.

Next step: Check your statement closing dates on your bank and retail cards, then make a payment before those dates.
